n400.title: N-400 interview
n400.lead: An officer may ask questions like these about your form. Answer as {name}. This part gets no score.
n400.sample.label: Sample answer for {name} (fictional)
n400.sample.note: This is only the made-up profile’s answer. Practice uses the fictional profile, so you never need to share real personal details here. In your real interview, you must answer truthfully about your own life.
coach.switch.label: AI coach (optional)
coach.switch.help: After each answer, get a short AI tip about your English. Off unless you turn it on.
coach.notice.title: Before you turn on the AI coach
coach.notice.text: When the AI coach is on, the words of each answer you type or say in this part are sent as text to Anthropic, an AI company, through Language Lab's server, to write feedback. Language Lab and Anthropic never receive your voice, only the words. Answer as the fictional person. Do not say real names, addresses, dates of birth, A-numbers or case details. In your real interview, you must answer truthfully about your own life. Language Lab checks for some numbers, but it cannot catch every personal detail. Language Lab does not keep your answers. Anthropic's privacy policy says how Anthropic handles them: anthropic.com/legal/privacy. The AI coach is off again when you start a new practice.
coach.choice.title: Would you like to use the AI coach?
coach.choice.lead: You can practice with or without it. You can turn it on or off later with the switch above the questions.
coach.label: AI-generated feedback
coach.followUp.label: A practice follow-up question:
coach.followUp.note: Practice an answer out loud if you like. This question is not recorded.
coach.tip.label: Tip about your English:
coach.feedback.scope: This checks how clear your English is. It does not say whether an answer is right or true.
coach.unavailable: AI feedback is not available right now. You can keep practicing.
coach.offNow: The AI coach is off for the rest of this practice.
coach.screened: This answer was not sent to the AI coach because it seems to contain {kind}. Answer as the fictional person, without real personal details.
coach.kind.dateOfBirth: a full date, such as a date of birth
coach.privacy: AI coach: off unless you turn it on in the N-400 part. When it is on, the text of each N-400 answer is sent to Anthropic through Language Lab's server to write feedback; no audio is sent. To limit use, the server counts requests with a daily, salted code made from your internet address; old counts are removed during later requests, normally within two days. Anthropic's privacy policy: anthropic.com/legal/privacy.
n400.failed: The next question did not load. Check your internet, then press “Start over”.
n400.done.title: Your answers
n400.done.lead: These are the words you gave. They are not scored.
voice.privacy: Voice uses your browser’s speech recognition. Depending on your browser, your voice may be processed by the browser’s maker. Language Lab does not send or save your voice. If you use “Record and compare”, the recording stays on this device, in memory, and is deleted when you go to the next sentence or close this page.
voice.consent.text: When you press “Tap to speak”, your browser’s speech recognition may send your voice to the browser’s maker, such as Google or Apple, to turn it into words. Language Lab does not send or save your voice. You can type your answer instead.
reading.title: Reading
reading.lead: Read the sentence out loud. You can type it if you prefer.
reading.done.passed: You read a sentence correctly. Reading is done.
reading.done.notPassed: That was the last sentence. More practice will help.
writing.title: Writing
writing.lead: Listen to the sentence, then type it.
writing.sentence: Listen, then type what you hear
writing.done.passed: You wrote a sentence correctly. Writing is done.
writing.done.notPassed: That was the last sentence. More practice will help.
compare.setting: A Language Lab practice setting based on the USCIS scoring guidelines, not a USCIS rule: every important word of the sentence must be there, in order. Short words such as “the” may be missing. Pauses and pronunciation are not scored.
compare.setting.writing: Writing: USCIS says spelling, capital letters and punctuation do not fail the writing test unless the sentence can no longer be understood. Here, small spelling slips still count, and longer words may have more. Capital letters and punctuation are not checked.
compare.vocab: The sentences use only words from the official USCIS reading and writing vocabulary lists.
writing.fallback: This browser cannot read aloud, so the sentence is shown here. Type it.
writing.hidden: The sentence stays hidden until you answer.
writing.show.help: If you cannot hear the sound, show the sentence and type it. It is checked the same way. Your report will say the sentence was shown.
writing.shown: The sentence is shown. Your report will say so.
civics.title: Civics
civics.lead: Answer out loud or type. Short answers are fine, but say the whole answer.
civics.stopped.correct: You reached the practice passing score, so the test stopped here.
civics.stopped.incorrect: The test stopped because too many answers need more practice.
civics.stopped.none: You have answered every question for this practice test.

home.how.2.title: Speak or type

home.how.3.text: You see if your answer counts, and what to practice next.

selfReview.title: Listen and compare
selfReview.help: Record yourself reading the sentence, then listen to your recording and to the sample. This is for you to compare by ear. It is not scored.
selfReview.recording: Recording. Read the sentence now, then press “Stop recording”.
selfReview.privacy: Your recording stays on this device. It is not sent anywhere or saved, and it is deleted when you go to the next sentence or leave this screen.
selfReview.unsupported: This browser cannot record your voice. You can still press “Tap to speak” or type.
selfReview.denied: The microphone is blocked, so recording cannot start. Allow the microphone for this site in your browser settings, then try again.
selfReview.error: Recording did not work this time. Try again.
compare.why.allWords: Every important word of the sentence was there, in order.
compare.note.variant.said: You said “{said}”. The sentence says “{expected}”. This still counts.
compare.note.variant.wrote: You wrote “{said}”. The sentence says “{expected}”. This still counts.
compare.note.different.said: You said “{said}”. The sentence says “{expected}”. That is a different word, so this does not count yet.
compare.note.different.wrote: You wrote “{said}”. The sentence says “{expected}”. That is a different word, so this does not count yet.
compare.note.spelling: You wrote “{said}”. The sentence has “{expected}”. This still counts. Check the spelling.
compare.note.missing: A word is missing: “{expected}”. This does not count yet.
compare.note.extra: You added “{said}”, which is not in the sentence. This does not count yet.
compare.note.extraStill: You added “{said}”, which is not in the sentence. This still counts.
compare.note.shortLeft: The short word “{expected}” was left out. This still counts.
compare.note.shortAdded: You added the short word “{said}”. This still counts.
compare.honest.heard: This result uses the words your phone or computer heard. If it heard you wrong, try again or type your answer.
compare.honest.typed: This result is based on the words you typed.
intro.special.help: This only changes the practice; nothing is saved or sent. The civics part then asks {asked} of the {bank} questions marked with a star (*) in the official list. In this practice, all {asked} are asked. The practice passing score is {pass} correct answers. For your own case, check uscis.gov: the age and the years count at the time of filing.
special.englishExempt: USCIS: at the time of filing, if you are 50 or older with 20 years as a permanent resident (50/20), or 55 or older with 15 years (55/15), you are exempt from the English requirement (reading, writing, speaking and understanding English), but you must still take the civics test. You may take it in your native language if you bring an interpreter. If you are 65 or older with at least 20 years (65/20), you are also exempt from English, and the officer uses specially designated civics test forms.
study.special.label: Only the questions for 65/20 (marked with a star)
study.special.dynamic: {count} of the {bank} questions have answers that change, such as who holds an office now. They are not shown here. Check them at uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates.
